LIS-A2-01.source:
Woman: Hello. Is the library workshop still open for registration?
Man: Yes. It is this Saturday at ten thirty in the morning.
Woman: Is it the workshop about growing herbs?
Man: That's right. Please bring a small container, but we will provide the seeds and soil.
Woman: Great. Is there a fee?
Man: No, it is free. Please arrive ten minutes early.
Woman: Thank you. I'll be there at ten twenty.

LIS-B1-01.source:
Host: Today we're talking about commuting. A local survey suggests that people often choose a route based on reliability, not just speed.
Guest: Yes. A train that takes thirty minutes every day can be less stressful than a car journey that takes twenty minutes on a good day but forty-five when traffic is heavy.
Host: What about cycling?
Guest: It is an option for shorter journeys, although safe routes and weather matter. Employers can also help by offering secure bicycle parking or flexible start times.
Host: So there's no single best choice for everyone?
Guest: Exactly. The useful question is which option fits a person's needs and is practical most days.

LIS-A1-01.source: Teacher: Hello, students. Here is a message about the photography club. The club meets this Thursday in Room 12. The meeting starts at four o'clock and finishes at five. Please bring a pencil and your phone or camera if you have one. You do not need to bring money. The club will provide paper and photo cards. New students should arrive ten minutes early to write their names on the club list. If you cannot come this week, the next meeting is on Thursday the fourteenth.

LIS-A2-02.source: Emma: Hi Ben. I'm calling about our science museum trip on Saturday. The bus was going to leave school at nine, but the driver has changed the time. It will leave at nine thirty now, so please meet at the school gate at nine fifteen. Ben: Okay. Do we still need to bring lunch? Emma: Yes. The museum café is closed for repairs, so bring a packed lunch. The school will provide water. Ben: Do we need money for the ticket? Emma: No, the teacher has already paid for the tickets. You only need money if you want to buy something in the gift shop. Ben: What time will we get back? Emma: Around three forty-five. Also, if your plans change and you cannot come, tell Ms Brown by Friday at twelve.

LIS-B1-02.source: Maya: We need to finish our presentation by Friday. The slides are almost done, but the survey chart is hard to read because I tried to show all sixty responses at once. Leo: Why don't we group similar responses into three categories? We can keep the full data in our notes in case the teacher asks about it. Maya: Good idea. I was also going to print colour copies for everyone, but that will be expensive. Leo: Let's make one large poster and share the full file online. The school printer can produce an A3 poster for free, but we have to send the file before four o'clock on Wednesday. Maya: Then I'll revise the chart tonight and send you a draft on Tuesday. Could you check it before lunch on Wednesday? Leo: Yes. I have football after school, so morning is better for me. Maya: One more thing. Twelve students skipped one survey question, and I'm worried people will think our data is incomplete. Leo: Add a note explaining that the question was optional. That makes the missing answers clear. Maya: Right. And during the presentation, let's focus on two main findings instead of reading every number.

LIS-A2-03.source:
Maya: Dad, I want to join one class at the sports centre this term. Badminton is on Tuesday at half past four, and climbing is on Thursday at five.

Dad: Which one costs less?

Maya: Badminton is twenty-four pounds for six weeks. Climbing is thirty pounds, but the centre provides the climbing shoes and safety equipment.

Dad: Do you need anything for badminton?

Maya: I need indoor sports shoes. I can borrow a racket for the first two lessons, but after that I should bring my own.

Dad: Tuesday is the day you have music club, isn’t it?

Maya: Yes. Music finishes at four fifteen, so getting to badminton by four thirty would be difficult.

Dad: Then climbing may be easier, even though it costs more.

Maya: I think so. Thursday is free, and I don’t need to buy special equipment at the start. I’ll choose climbing.

LIS-B1-04.source:
Nina: We need to decide the plan for our next school podcast. I still think we should interview Ms Patel about the community garden. She can explain how students helped design it.

Omar: I like the topic, but she can only meet us on Wednesday after school. Our edited episode is due Friday morning.

Nina: That gives us Thursday to edit. It’s tight, but possible if we keep the interview short.

Omar: My bigger worry is the recording room. The drama club has booked it on Wednesday. We could record in the library, but there may be people walking past.

Nina: What if we use the small study room at the back? It isn’t completely silent, but we can put a sign on the door and sit close to the microphone.

Omar: That could work. I was going to suggest changing the topic, but I’d rather keep the garden interview if the sound is clear enough.

Nina: Let’s prepare five questions instead of eight. Then the interview should take about ten minutes, and we can start editing the same evening.

Omar: Okay. So we keep Ms Patel, use the study room, and make a shorter interview. If the room is too noisy when we arrive, we’ll record her answers on Thursday lunchtime instead.

Nina: Good. It’s not our perfect plan, but it gives us a backup.

LIS-A1-02.source: Teacher: Hello, class. Here is a quick change for Thursday's English club. We usually meet in Room 7, but another class needs that room this week. Please go to Room 14 instead. The club still starts at four o'clock and finishes at five. Bring your English notebook and a pencil. You do not need your course book because I will give you a short reading sheet. Please arrive five minutes early so we can begin on time.

LIS-B1-03.source: Nina: We still need to prepare for Friday's history quiz. Shall we meet after school tomorrow? Omar: I can, but I have basketball practice at five, so I need to leave by four thirty. Nina: Then how about meeting in the library at three thirty? We could spend twenty minutes reviewing dates and then practise the longer questions. Omar: That works. I made flashcards for the dates, but I have not finished the chapter summary. Nina: I can bring my summary. Could you bring the teacher's practice sheet? Omar: Yes. Should we invite Maya too? She said she wanted help with the longer answers. Nina: Good idea, but let's message her now so she has time to reply. Omar: One more thing: the library computers are often busy after school. Do we need one? Nina: Probably not. The practice sheet and our notes should be enough. Omar: Great. I'll bring the sheet and flashcards, and you bring the summary. We'll meet by the library entrance at three thirty.

LIS-A1-03.source:
A: Good morning. What would you like today?
B: Two cheese rolls and one small apple pie, please.
A: I'm sorry. We only have one cheese roll left. We have fresh tomato sandwiches, though.
B: That's fine. I'll take one cheese roll and one tomato sandwich. No pie today.
A: Of course. Would you like a drink?
B: No, thank you. How much is that?
A: Five pounds altogether.
B: Here you are. I'm taking lunch to the park.
A: Thank you. Enjoy your lunch!

LIS-A1-04.source: A new family lives in the flat above ours. Their daughter is called Mia. She is twelve years old, and she moved here last week. Mia likes drawing animals, but she doesn't like playing football. On Tuesday, she showed me a picture of a little fox. It was beautiful. We are going to the playground together on Friday afternoon. I want to show her the big trees behind the swings. She also wants to meet my little sister, who loves drawing too.

LIS-A1-05.source:
A: Excuse me. Have you seen a blue hat?
B: Maybe. Is it a dark blue hat with a white star?
A: No, mine is light blue, with a small green flower.
B: I saw a hat like that near the drinking fountain this morning.
A: I went there, but it wasn't on the bench.
B: The school office has a box of lost things. Let's look there.
A: Oh, here it is, next to a red scarf!
B: Great. Is that your name inside?
A: Yes, it says Anna. Thank you for helping me.

LIS-A2-04.source:
A: Have you checked the train times for our trip to the coast?
B: Yes, but there's a problem. The ten fifteen train has been delayed by forty minutes.
A: Oh no. We wanted to arrive before lunchtime. Is there another one?
B: There's a train at ten thirty from platform four. We have to change at Westford, but it should still get us there by twelve.
A: The original train was direct, wasn't it?
B: It was. The new route takes a little more effort, but it's faster today.
A: Let's take the ten thirty, then. Have you bought the tickets?
B: Not yet. I'll buy them on my phone while you check the platform number.
A: Platform four. Got it. We'd better leave for the station now.

LIS-A2-05.source: Hello, this is a reminder about the children's art exhibition at the town hall. The exhibition opens on Saturday morning, but please note that the opening time has changed. The doors will open at half past ten, not ten o'clock, because the artists need extra time to arrange their work. You can still visit until four in the afternoon. Entry is free, and families are welcome. Please use the side entrance while the front steps are being repaired. If you would like to take photographs, ask an organiser first. Some of the young artists do not want pictures of their work posted online. We hope to see you there.

LIS-A2-06.source:
A: Your bicycle is making a strange noise. Are you still going on the ride tomorrow?
B: I hope so. The brakes work, but the back wheel keeps rubbing against the frame.
A: That doesn't sound safe. Could you take it to the repair shop this afternoon?
B: I called them. They can check it at three, but they can't promise to finish before closing.
A: What if you borrow my brother's bicycle for tomorrow? He is away for the weekend.
B: Thanks, but it's too small for me. I think I'll wait until my own bicycle is fixed.
A: That makes sense. We could walk by the river instead.
B: Good idea. Let's meet at the bridge at nine, unless it rains.

LIS-B1-05.source:
A: Did you see the new borrowing service at the community centre? You can borrow things like camping equipment and simple tools, not just books.
B: I saw the notice, but I'm not sure it will work. What happens if someone breaks an expensive tool?
A: Members sign an agreement and leave a small deposit. If the item comes back in good condition, they get the deposit back.
B: That's reasonable, although someone still has to check everything between loans.
A: Volunteers will do that. The centre is starting with a small collection, so they can learn what people actually need.
B: I like the idea of sharing equipment instead of buying something you use once a year. But what if the thing you want is already on loan?
A: There's an online booking calendar. It won't solve every problem, but at least you can plan ahead.
B: In that case, I'd like to try it. I need a tent for one weekend, and buying a new one would be wasteful.
A: Let's register together after school. I want to borrow a set of gardening tools.

LIS-B1-06.source: Last month, our class organised a one-day pop-up sale to raise money for new sports equipment. At first, we planned to sell only homemade snacks. However, a survey showed that many students wanted second-hand books as well, so we added a book table. On the morning of the event, we discovered that the room was smaller than we had expected. We moved the snack table outside, where more people could see it. By lunchtime, most of the books had sold, but the snacks were selling slowly. Instead of lowering every price, we offered a small discount on snack boxes bought by families. That helped, and we reached our fundraising target just before closing. The most useful lesson wasn't about money. We learned to ask people what they wanted, respond calmly when plans changed, and keep simple records. Next time, we'll check the room size before making the layout.

LIS-B1-07.source:
A: Someone posted a photograph of the river near our town. The water looks bright green. People are saying a factory must be putting chemicals into it.
B: That's worrying, but do we know when the picture was taken?
A: No. The post doesn't give a date. It just says, "Look what happened today."
B: Could the colour be caused by the camera or by something natural? We shouldn't guess from one photograph.
A: You're right. I nearly shared it because the comments sounded so certain.
B: Let's check whether the local environmental office has reported anything. We could also look for a second photograph from a reliable source.
A: I've found a notice from last year about harmless green dye used to test the movement of water. But that doesn't prove this is the same situation.
B: Exactly. It gives us another possibility, not a final answer.
A: I'll wait for a current official update instead of spreading the claim. If there's a real problem, we can share confirmed information and ask what people should do.
B: Good plan. Being careful isn't the same as ignoring the problem.
